queue.workResult: Applied Skill 02 to all seven same-date signals with problem-first admission, release-boundary, evidence-sufficiency, source-concentration, semantic-concentration, primary-research utilization and research-problem deduplication against the 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-05 Research Plans. Digital Employee selected Q-20260906-01 from the controlled cost-aware multi-agent routing study: the research object separates failure-risk admission from protocol-specific collaboration value and token-cost budget rather than treating escalation as a binary 'add more agents' switch. Industry Architecture selected Q-20260906-02 from the primary agent-based supply-network study: the object is phase-specific resilience under trust-mediated coordination, not eventual recovery as a single terminal metric. Open-source Engineering selected Q-20260906-03 as a cross-implementation problem anchored in OpenAI Agents SDK stable agent-graph identity and strengthened by Codex managed-worktree fork re-admission: durable state needs stable principal identity, but a workspace/session transition must still re-evaluate destination trust, configuration and execution authority. SIG-20260906-001 remains a strong failure-evidence candidate but loses the Digital Employee slot to the deeper paired empirical evidence in SIG-20260906-006; SIG-20260906-002 remains a single-vendor announcement candidate; SIG-20260906-003 is retained as cross-support for Q-20260906-03 rather than selected again. SIG-20260906-005 is rejected as DUPLICATE_RESEARCH_PROBLEM because exact target-resource authority at call time materially overlaps the September 2 layered connector-authority object. Queue performed no Deep Reading, Research Analysis, article writing, visualization, Production or Publication.

triage.candidate: Running state versus executable readiness under MCP dependency failure
triage.researchQuestion: Which dependency-admission state must be proven before a digital worker may be called executable rather than merely Running?
triage.selectionReason: Strong reproducible failure evidence with staff fault attribution, but the Digital Employee slot is awarded to SIG-20260906-006 because its paired protocol study provides deeper comparative evidence and direct cost-governance findings.

triage.candidate: Shared content-exclusion enforcement at agent context admission
triage.researchQuestion: At which shared context boundary must administrator exclusions be enforced so every agentic surface sees the same admissible evidence set?
triage.selectionReason: Bounded and useful context-policy mechanism, but the same-date pool provides only one official vendor announcement.

triage.candidate: Managed-worktree fork re-admission across trust, configuration and session state
triage.researchQuestion: Which destination facts must be re-admitted before conversation history and state can cross into a different checkout?
triage.selectionReason: Strong complementary implementation evidence, retained as cross-support for Q-20260906-03 so the same identity/transition problem is not selected twice.

triage.candidate: Stable agent-graph identity across persistence and resume
triage.researchQuestion: What stable principal identity must survive serialization and nested agent/tool relationships so restored authority and tool state bind to the intended agent?
triage.selectionReason: Stable graph identity and destination fork re-admission are complementary implementations of one durable-transition problem: identity continuity is necessary for state continuity but must not imply automatic authority continuity.

triage.candidate: Bearer-token resource binding for MCP call-time authority
triage.researchQuestion: Must a valid token also be bound to the exact target resource before an MCP call is authorized?
triage.selectionReason: Credible implementation evidence, but the September 2 layered connector-authority object already made target-resource authority and call-time revalidation an explicit research dimension.

triage.candidate: Cost-aware multi-agent protocol routing after failure-risk admission
triage.researchQuestion: How should a digital worker choose collaboration topology and cost budget after a failure-risk gate indicates that escalation may help?
triage.selectionReason: Primary paired study directly separates failure prediction from protocol-specific value and cost, producing the strongest same-date Digital Employee evidence.

triage.candidate: Phase-specific resilience under trust-mediated multi-agent coordination
triage.researchQuestion: Which phase-specific resilience and trust measures are required when eventual recovery can hide poor shock absorption, adaptation or containment?
triage.selectionReason: Primary industry application study supplies comparative phase, policy and network evidence and creates a distinct operational-resilience architecture question.
